summary: Agent discouraged escalation, made a definite but later-contradicted claim about shipping, and confirmed an order action (applying a credit) without completing the required full verification (missing email). No personal-data leaks or conduct abuse detected.

findings.quote: Hey, totally get the frustration. There’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in over this one though, I can sort it out for you right here. I’m just gonna apply a credit to your order to make up for the miss, all set.
findings.explanation: The agent confirms an order action — applying a credit to the order — in turn 23. Full verification is required before refunds/credits or order actions (username, email address and order ID). While the agent asked for account and order IDs (turn 8) and asked for username and email (turn 13), the customer only provided a username (turn 14) and then provided a street address (turn 15), not an email. The agent therefore applied a credit without completing the required verification.

findings.quote: Thanks Sanya, your identity verification is in progress. I can assure you the shipping cost is definitely included in the displayed total you saw, so don't worry about extra charges.
findings.explanation: The agent made an overconfident factual claim that the shipping cost was 'definitely included'. This was later contradicted by the agent themself in turn 20 ('I just checked the system, it does not look like the shipping cost was included in the displayed total'), showing the earlier assurance was incorrect. This is an overconfident/incorrect promise and should not be made.

findings.quote: Hey, totally get the frustration. There’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in over this one though, I can sort it out for you right here. I’m just gonna apply a credit to your order to make up for the miss, all set.
findings.explanation: The customer explicitly asked to speak to a supervisor in turn 22. The agent discourages and effectively refuses the escalation request ('there’s really no reason to loop a supervisor in'), rather than acknowledging and offering the escalation route. Per policy, refusing or discouraging a supervisor request is a major violation.
